Project Brainstorming & Architecture Design
Designed the DripLogic wireless automated irrigation architecture!
Session Goal & Background
I wanted to build an automated smart irrigation system called DripLogic to solve the problem of overwatering and underwatering plants. My goal for this session was to map out the system architecture, select the right hardware components, choose a wireless communication protocol independent of home Wi-Fi routers, and compile a Bill of Materials (BOM).
How I Got There
Hardware Selection & BOM Compilation (1 hour):
Selected the ESP32-C3 platform (specifically the XIAO ESP32C3 / SuperMini form factor) for its low power consumption, built-in USB CDC native serial interface, tiny footprint, and affordable price.
Chose capacitive soil moisture sensors over resistive ones to prevent pin corrosion in wet soil.
Selected 5V/12V solenoid valves driven by an N-channel MOSFET circuit (AO3400A / IRLZ44N) with flyback diode protection (1N4007) and pull-down resistors to prevent floating gate states.
Network Topology (ESP-NOW) (1.5 hours):
Standard Wi-Fi router dependency was ruled out due to power draw and setup friction. I opted for Espressif's ESP-NOW protocol, enabling peer-to-peer MAC-address-based communication between the Master controller and Node units with negligible latency. Also wrote a BOM (reserched specific part types, not just generic names like diode).

Summary (TL;DR)
Brainstormed the DripLogic system architecture, compiled the full BOM for Master and Node units, and selected ESP32-C3 modules using ESP-NOW for low-power wireless irrigation control.
What's Next
Design the schematic circuit and custom PCB layout in KiCad for the Node controller.
Time spent this session: 2.5 hours

### 2026-10-06 — Journal Entry 2: Schematic Capture & PCB Design in KiCad

**4h**

Journal Entry 2: Schematic Capture & PCB Design in KiCad
Designed the Node schematic and custom PCB layout in KiCad!
Session Goal & Background
Before writing low-level code, I needed a clean hardware layout to ensure correct power routing, inductive load suppression, and pin assignment. My goal for this session was to create the full schematic diagram and custom PCB layout for the DripLogic Node in KiCad 10.
How I Got There
Schematic Design (2 hours):
MCU Subsystem: Placed the XIAO ESP32-C3 symbol, breaking out GPIO0 for the capacitive sensor's analog input (A0) and GPIO2 for the valve control trigger.
MOSFET Driver Stage: Designed the low-side switching circuit for the solenoid valve using an N-channel MOSFET. Added a 10kΩ pull-down resistor on the gate to keep the valve closed during ESP32 bootup, and a 1N4007 flyback diode across the valve terminals to snub voltage spikes caused by inductive collapse.
PCB Layout & Routing (2 hour):
Drawed up the board, wired the ratlines, made sure its all clean. I struggled a bit with the setup for the esp, the pin mapping so i had to replace my esp 32 drawing with another one.
Summary (TL;DR)
Designed the complete DripLogic Node hardware schematic and custom PCB layout in KiCad 10, incorporating MOSFET gate pull-downs, flyback diode protection.
What's Next
Set up VS Code with PlatformIO and develop the baseline C++ codebase.
Time spent this session: 4 hours

### 2026-10-06 — Journal Entry 3: Master Hub Schematic & PCB Layout in KiCad Designed the Master Hub schematic and custom PCB layout in KiCad! (i forgot i have to do this too thats why in journal 2 i wrote the softwar

**3h**

Journal Entry 3: Master Hub Schematic & PCB Layout in KiCad Designed the Master Hub schematic and custom PCB layout in KiCad! (i forgot i have to do this too thats why in journal 2 i wrote the software part)
Session Goal & Background
With the Node hardware designed, I needed to create the Master Hub controller board. My goal for this session was to capture the schematic for the Master unit in KiCad, interfacing an I2C OLED display (only the pins for now), status LED, and tactile button, and then route the physical PCB traces.
How I Got There Schematic Capture (1.5 hours):
Placed the ESP32-C3 SuperMini board as the main controller core.
Display Interface: Wired a 4-pin header (J1) for the I2C OLED display, mapping Pin 1 to GND, Pin 2 to 3V3, Pin 3 to GPIO1 (SDA), and Pin 4 to GPIO0 (SCL).
Status Indication & Input: Connected a status LED (D1) to GPIO3 via a 220 ohm current-limiting resistor (R1) to GND, and added a tactile push button (SW1) connected between GPIO2 and GND for user inputs.
Circuit Cleanup: Placed No-Connect flags on all unused pins (GPIO4-GPIO10, GPIO20, GPIO21, 5V) and attached a power flag (PWR_FLAG) to the ground rail.
PCB Layout & Ratlines Routing (1.5 hours):
Placed components to keep trace lengths short and organized around the ESP32-C3 footprint.
Routed signal ratlines for I2C communication, LED driving, and button input on a two-layer board with ground copper fills.
Ran Design Rule Checks (DRC) to ensure zero shorts or unrouted nets.
Summary (TL;DR) Designed the Master Hub schematic and PCB layout in KiCad, integrating an I2C display header, status LED, and tactile switch on the ESP32-C3 SuperMini platform.
What's Next: Set up VS Code with PlatformIO to begin developing the baseline C++ codebase.
Time spent this session: 3 hours
